_renderer: mapsRenderer picks WHICH KEY SET owns the one map draw path (mhud_draw_pane_full). 'unified' -- the shipped value -- means spatialMode owns it and the LEGACY hudRadar/hudMap/radarX/radarY/radarSize keys are NOT read, so turning a Legacy toggle off can no longer leave nothing drawing (the reported bug). 'legacy' hands ownership back to the old pair and spatialMode is not read. 'auto' is what a config written before this key gets: legacy owns it only while spatialMode is unwritten, which is the migration behaviour and is exactly the state the bug lived in. The loser is deselected, never unbound -- switching applies live.
_both: spatialMode `both` draws the minimap AND the radar at once -- two panes in one dispatch, through the ONE pane renderer, so they cannot drift apart. It is the only mode entitled to more than one pane, and that entitlement is a NUMBER the draw ledger compares against (paneCallsOver counts panes above it, paneCallsUnder panes below it), never an exemption from the check. `both` is also the only mode in which radarAnchor/radarX/radarY/radarSize are live geometry rather than migration-only keys: the two panes need two rects or they land exactly on top of each other. radarAnchor defaults to `manual`, which is the historical absolute placement, so taking this build moves nobody's radar.
_markers: The four marker kinds are declared as SEPARATE rows and every one is implemented=false, for the reason the umbrella `markers` key already carried: on build 1.1.0.1.46777 no field offset has been measured for the loot, extract, quest or dead lists, and sp/world.nim walks the ALIVE players list only. Naming them per kind does not make any of them draw -- it makes the refusal specific about which measurement is missing, instead of one switch that silently does nothing.
_drawVerdict: drawVerdictFrames bounds the draw verdict. `a surface is selected and nothing has drawn YET` is true on frame 3 and is a defect on frame 3000, and unbounded it is a verdict no input could falsify. The clock is dispatches that got PAST the in-raid lifecycle gate, counted by the C renderer, so menu frames cannot spend it; once it is exhausted the maps diag says FAIL and names the mode. It may be large. It may not be infinite.
_widget: ONE spatial widget replaces the separate hudRadar/hudMap surfaces. spatialMode 'auto' means: derive the mode from the legacy hudRadar/hudMap/heading keys above, so an existing config keeps the surface it had (a migrated radar also carries radarX/radarY/radarSize into mapX/mapY/mapSize). Pick any other mode and the legacy keys stop being consulted.
_placement: widgetAnchor 'manual' keeps mapX/mapY as the absolute top-left, which is what every existing config already means -- nobody's widget moves. Any corner value turns mapX/mapY into an INSET from that corner, resolved each frame against the MEASURED back buffer and clamped on-screen.
_detail: detail is a PRESET over drawArt / mapGrid / northPip, not a filter on them. custom -- the shipped value -- means those three switches decide and this key changes nothing. low = no art, no grid, no pip (the cheapest pane). medium = grid + pip, no art. high = all three FORCED on. Because the presets override rather than AND, all four values are distinguishable outcomes instead of `high` being a second name for `custom`; when a preset overrides a switch you set by hand the host log says so once, by name. It deliberately does NOT cap the contact count: the contact array has no distance ordering, so a cap would drop an arbitrary subset -- possibly the nearest enemy. Use radiusM to cut contacts by distance.
_enemyVisibility: always is the only policy this build can carry out. shootOnly (draw a hostile only once it has FIRED) is DECLARED so the request is named, and is REFUSED at read time with the reason in the host log -- never applied as a silent no-op. There is no shot signal: this mod does not consume mods/admin's feed at all (it does its own IL2CPP walk in sp/world.nim), and nothing in the repo publishes a per-contact last-fired time -- admin's NewRecoilShotEffect+0x11 is the LOCAL player's own weapon. It needs a measured field offset for a bot's last-shot time on build 1.1.0.1.46777, and none has been taken.
_fullscreen: The full-screen map, on a key. hotkeys is OFF by default: with it off NOTHING is polled -- GameAssembly is not even looked up -- and the key does nothing. Turning it on binds UnityEngine.Input::GetKeyDown at a byte-verified RVA and reads one key per Unity tick. It never CAPTURES input, so there is nothing that can stay captured if it faults; press the key again or Escape to close.
_activation: fullscreenActivation is PRESS (a toggle: one press opens, the next or Escape closes -- the historical behaviour and the default, so nobody's key changes) or HOLD (open exactly while the key is held, closed the frame it is released). PRESS reads UnityEngine.Input::GetKeyDown @0x531EB80; HOLD reads UnityEngine.Input::GetKey @0x531EAE0, a SEPARATELY byte-verified RVA with its own bind state, so a prologue mismatch on one cannot disarm the other and the diag names which refused. HOLD is a LEVEL read and is ASSIGNED, never toggled -- there is no accumulated state that a missed release edge could leave stuck open over a raid. Changing this while the map is open closes it, in both directions.
_notImplementedYet: markers is still declared implemented=false in maps.nim and the settings UI marks it so -- it is NOT a silent no-op: it needs a field offset for the loot/extract/corpse/quest lists on build 1.1.0.1.46777 (none has been measured). heading IS now implemented: the player VIEW facing is measured (MovementContext._lookDirection) and rotates both surfaces heading-up. One ABI limit remains and is stated in the schema and the diag: the region's textured quad is axis-aligned, so heading-up cannot rotate the baked map ART and falls back to a rotating grid+blips; turn heading OFF to see the artwork north-up.
